resources.string: Briefly took over the screen while you were using another app, or right after unlocking. This is how out-of-context (disruptive) ads behave and it is banned by Google Play policy.
Opened a screen right after a phone call ended. Adware listens for calls ending to push full-screen ads.
Has the \"Display over other apps\" permission and stays busy in the background while you rarely open it. Overlays are the most abused permission by adware.
Has no icon in your app drawer yet is active in the background. Hiding the icon is a classic adware trick to avoid being uninstalled.
Kept a foreground service alive for hours while you barely used it. This keeps the CPU awake and drains battery.
Woke up or launched screens while your screen was off during the night.
Transferred a lot of data while in the background. Android vitals flags more than 50 MB of mobile data per day as excessive.
Posted an unusually high number of notifications.
Has an enabled accessibility service, which can read your screen and act on your behalf. Only keep it for apps you fully trust.
Is registered as device administrator, which makes it harder to uninstall.
Is exempt from battery optimisation and works heavily in the background.
Keeps a very large cache. Clearing it frees space and can speed up the phone.

Didn\'t come from an app store: it was installed from a link in a chat or email, or from a downloaded file. That\'s how scam apps reach phones, especially ones that ask for access to your messages or screen.
Can read your text messages or notifications, where bank and login codes arrive. Fraud apps ask for this to take over accounts. Remove the access unless you fully trust the app.

A remote-control app was installed recently. Scammers posing as your bank or tech support ask you to install one so they can watch your screen. If someone asked you to install it, hang up and uninstall it.
Didn\'t come from an app store, yet is named like a well-known app or part of Android (\"System update\", a bank, WhatsApp). Fake apps borrow trusted names.
Is allowed to install other apps. Malware uses this to download more apps after it\'s installed. Turn it off in Settings unless you need it.

Was installed from outside an app store shortly after SMS Toolbox flagged a text with a link as a possible scam. Fake parcel, bank and \"security\" apps spread this way. If a text or a caller asked you to install it, uninstall it now and never type a code it asks for.
Froze several times today and showed \"App isn\'t responding\". Frequent ANRs make the phone feel slow.
Crashed several times today. Updating, clearing its cache or reinstalling it usually helps.
